images.title: Divide, stop, check
images.purpose: Recap the whole prime splitting routine in three steps, ending with multiplying the primes back to check.
images.composition: Three rounded panels in a single row across the frame, joined by two grey arrows, each panel holding one small step with white space between them.
exact_structure: Panel 1 (teal #0072B2 border), heading Divide by a prime: a mini division ladder for 60 with rows 2 | 60, 2 | 30, 3 | 15, then 5 at the bottom.
Panel 2 (amber #E69F00 border), heading Stop at a prime: the single number 5 circled in reddish purple #CC79A7.
Panel 3 (green #009E73 border), heading Multiply back: the line 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 60 with a green tick.
Exactly 2 grey #6B7280 arrows: panel 1 to panel 2, panel 2 to panel 3.
rejection: any ladder row that does not divide exactly (60 ÷ 2 = 30, 30 ÷ 2 = 15, 15 ÷ 3 = 5)
a check product that does not equal 60
images.takeaway: Divide by primes until a prime is left, then multiply the primes back to make sure you get the number.
images.description: Three panels: a division ladder for 60, the stopping prime 5 circled, and the check 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 60.
images.context: Shown beside the practice tool for splitting numbers into primes.
images.teaching_notes: Use the three panels as a checklist before and after each practice number.

image_decisions.why: A compact three step recap guides the practice routine, including the check.
